column1: g1|2|だれの・ね・よ|Whose; seeking agreement; offering information.|だれの + N; sentence + ね / よ|ね invites shared recognition; よ presents information the listener may not know. Intonation changes how forceful they sound.|これはだれのノートですか。私のですよ。|Whose notebook is this? It is mine.

g1|3|動詞の活用・語順・助詞|Verb groups, word order and core particles.|Topic は; object を; destination に/へ; action location で; companion と; predicate last|Ru-verbs drop る before ます. U-verbs change the final u-row sound to the i-row; する→します and 来る→来ます. Particle roles matter more than a rigid English word order.|私は図書館で日本語を勉強します。|I study Japanese at the library.

g1|3|時間のに・頻度の副詞|When and how often an action happens.|Clock/calendar time + に; 毎日 / 今日 usually without に; あまり / 全然 + negative|Use に with a specific time such as 七時. Relative words such as 明日 normally stand alone. あまり describes low frequency or degree with a negative.|日曜日に泳ぎますが、平日はあまり泳ぎません。|I swim on Sundays, but do not swim much on weekdays.

g1|4|あります・います|Existence and possession.|Place に + thing が ある; person/animal が いる|Use いる for animate beings and ある for things. The location of existence takes に, unlike the place where an action occurs, which takes で.|庭に猫がいます。木もあります。|There is a cat in the garden. There is also a tree.

g1|4|時間・数量・と|Duration, quantities, also and together with.|Duration without に; N と N; person と + action; quantity + も|三時間 is a duration, 三時 is a clock time. と can list nouns or mark a companion; たくさん can modify an action or appear as たくさんのN.|友達と三時間話しました。|I talked with a friend for three hours.

g1|5|い形容詞・な形容詞|Adjective predicates, past forms and noun modification.|い: 高い→高くない→高かった→高くなかった; な: 静かだ / 静かなN|いい conjugates with よい: よくない、よかった. Do not attach だ directly to an い-adjective. な appears before a noun, not before です.|昨日は寒かったです。今日は静かな店で休みます。|It was cold yesterday. Today I will rest in a quiet cafe.

g1|5|数え方・数量の位置|Counting objects and people.|Number + appropriate counter; N を + quantity + verb|Counters depend on the object. General counters include 一つ、二つ、三つ; people include 一人、二人、三人. A quantity can follow the particle without の.|りんごを三つ買いました。|I bought three apples.

g1|6|て形・順序・禁止|Connect actions and state prohibitions.|Vて、V; Vてはいけない|U-verbs: うつる→って、むぶぬ→んで、く→いて、ぐ→いで、す→して. 行く→行って. Ru-verbs drop る + て. Requests, sequence and prohibitions all use this form.|朝ご飯を食べて、学校に行きます。ここで走ってはいけません。|I eat breakfast and go to school. You must not run here.

g1|7|〜ている：動作・結果|An ongoing action or a continuing resulting state.|Vて + いる|読んでいる is usually ongoing reading. 結婚している is being married. The interpretation depends on the verb; the negative of 知っている is normally 知らない.|妹は今勉強しています。兄は大阪に住んでいます。|My younger sister is studying now. My older brother lives in Osaka.
g1|7|人数を数える|Count people.|一人（ひとり）、二人（ふたり）、三人（さんにん）、何人（なんにん）|四人 is よにん. Use a counter after the relevant noun/particle, or use number + の + noun.|教室に学生が四人います。|There are four students in the classroom.

g1|8|普通形・と思う・と言う|Plain forms in conversation and quotation.|Plain clause + と思う / と言う; noun/な-adjective + だと|Plain negative: 食べない、書かない、しない、来ない. ある→ない. Keep だ when quoting an affirmative noun predicate. Casual questions often use rising intonation without か.|明日は雨だと思います。友達もそう言っていました。|I think it will rain tomorrow. My friend said so too.

g1|8|が・何か・何も|Identify a subject, something or nothing.|Question-word subject + が; 何か; 何も + negative|が often introduces or identifies the subject. は frames a topic or contrast. 何も does not mean nothing by itself; it combines with a negative predicate.|だれが来ますか。私は何も知りません。|Who is coming? I do not know anything.

g1|9|過去の普通形・名詞修飾|Plain past forms and clauses before nouns.|Vた / Vなかった; plain clause + N|Past plain forms follow the te-form sound changes with た/だ. A modifying clause comes before its noun without a relative pronoun. Noun/な-adjective past is だった.|昨日買った本は面白かったです。|The book I bought yesterday was interesting.

g1|10|比較・一番|Compare two or several items.|AはBより…; AとBとどちらが…; group で何/どれが一番…|より marks the comparison standard. のほうが identifies the preferred or higher-degree side. Choose the question word for the kind of item being compared.|電車のほうがバスより速いです。|The train is faster than the bus.

g1|10|名詞の代わりの「の」|Replace an understood noun.|い-adjective + の; な-adjective + なの; possessor + の|The omitted noun must be recoverable from context. 赤いの means the red one; 私の means mine. This の is different from explanatory のです.|青いのより、赤いのが好きです。|I prefer the red one to the blue one.

g1|10|どこか・どこにも・で|Somewhere, nowhere and a means or cost.|どこかに; どこにも + negative; means / total cost + で|Particles combine with question-word expressions: どこかへ行く, どこへも行かない. で can mark a means or the total amount used.|休みはどこにも行きません。二千円でこの本を買いました。|I will not go anywhere on my day off. I bought this book for two thousand yen.

g1|11|〜たり〜たりする・や|Give non-exhaustive examples.|Vた + り、Vた + りする; NやN|たり lists representative activities, not a strict sequence. Put tense on the final する. や lists nouns and implies other examples exist.|休みの日は料理をしたり、本を読んだりします。|On days off I do things such as cooking and reading.

g1|12|〜んです|Explain background or ask for an explanation.|Plain form + んです; N/な-adjective + なんです|Use it when the reason or background is relevant to the conversation. It is not required in every factual statement.|今日は早く帰ります。試験があるんです。|I am going home early today. I have an exam.

g1|12|〜ほうがいい|Give advice.|Vた + ほうがいい; Vない + ほうがいい|The affirmative uses the past form even when advising about the future. It can sound strong, so consider the relationship and situation.|今日は早く寝たほうがいいですよ。|You should go to bed early today.

g2|13|〜そうです：様子|An appearance-based impression.|い-adjective without い + そう; な-adjective stem + そう; verb stem + そう|おいしそう means looks tasty; おいしいそうだ reports what someone said. いい→よさそう、ない→なさそう. V-stemそう can signal an imminent event.|このケーキはおいしそうです。雨が降りそうです。|This cake looks tasty. It looks like it will rain.
g2|13|期間に回数|Frequency within a period.|Period + に + number of times|一週間に二回 means twice a week, not for two weeks. 回 counts occurrences.|週に三回、日本語を練習しています。|I practice Japanese three times a week.

g2|14|あげる・くれる・もらう|Giving and receiving objects.|Giver は receiver に Nをあげる/くれる; receiver は giver に/から Nをもらう|くれる describes giving toward the speaker or their in-group. もらう makes the recipient the subject. The forms encode viewpoint, not just politeness.|妹が私に本をくれました。私は妹に本をもらいました。|My younger sister gave me a book. I received a book from her.

g2|14|数量＋も・しか〜ない|A surprisingly large amount or a restricted amount.|Number + も; number + しか + negative|も emphasizes as many/as much as. しか requires a negative predicate but the meaning is only that amount.|一時間も待ちました。お金は五百円しかありません。|I waited a whole hour. I have only five hundred yen.

g2|15|〜ておく|Prepare in advance or leave something in a state.|Vて + おく|The action serves a later purpose. Leaving a state unchanged is another use. Casual contractions include 買っておく→買っとく.|明日のために資料を読んでおきます。|I will read the materials in advance for tomorrow.

g2|16|〜てあげる・てくれる・てもらう|Describe beneficial actions from a viewpoint.|Vて + あげる / くれる / もらう|先生が教えてくれた makes the teacher the giver; 先生に教えてもらった makes me the recipient. Offering てあげる directly can sound presumptuous.|友達に作文を見てもらいました。|I had a friend look over my composition.

g2|16|〜ていただけませんか|Politely request a favor.|Vて + いただけませんか|The potential negative question asks whether you could receive the favor. It is more indirect than てください.|もう一度説明していただけませんか。|Could you please explain it one more time?

g2|16|〜てすみません・なくてすみません|Apologize for an action or omission.|Vて + すみません; Vなくて + すみません|For not doing something use the negative connecting form なくて, not the instruction pattern ないでください.|連絡が遅くなってすみません。|I am sorry for contacting you late.

g2|17|〜って・みたいです|Casual quotation and inference/resemblance.|Plain clause + って; V/い-adjective plain or N/な-adjective stem + みたいだ|って can quote or report speech; it can also mark a topic. みたいだ expresses resemblance or an inference, not simply quoted news.|店は今日休みだって。だれもいないみたいです。|I heard the shop is closed today. It seems no one is there.

g2|17|〜前に・〜てから|Before and after an action.|V dictionary + 前に; Nの前に; Vてから|Use dictionary form before 前に even for a past main event. てから emphasizes that the first action precedes the second.|出かける前に電話しました。帰ってから勉強します。|I called before going out. I will study after returning.

g2|18|〜てしまう|Completion or an unwanted result.|Vて + しまう|Context determines whether it is simple completion or regret. Spoken forms include ちゃう and じゃう.|大切なメールを消してしまいました。|I accidentally deleted an important email.

g2|18|〜ながら|Do two actions at the same time.|Vます-stem + ながら|For this simultaneous-action use, both actions share a subject. The main action comes last. Concessive ながら is a separate construction.|音楽を聞きながら料理します。|I cook while listening to music.

g2|19|〜てくれてありがとう・〜てよかった|Thank someone or express relief.|Vてくれて + ありがとう; Vて / Vなくて + よかった|くれて makes the helpful person's action explicit. よかった evaluates a situation favorably after it occurs.|手伝ってくれてありがとう。間に合ってよかったです。|Thank you for helping. I am glad we made it in time.

g2|19|〜はずです|An expectation supported by a reason.|V/い-adjective plain + はず; Nの / な-adjectiveな + はず|It expresses an expectation, not a guarantee. はずがない denies the possibility; はずだった can express an expectation that was not met.|今日は祝日なので、銀行は休みのはずです。|It is a holiday today, so the bank should be closed.

g2|20|丁重語・謙譲語|Speak modestly and respectfully.|参る・申す・おります; おV-stemする / ごNする|Humble language can show respect toward the recipient of an action; extra-modest language is polite toward the listener. Do not apply mechanical honorific prefixes to every verb.|私は田中と申します。資料をお送りします。|My name is Tanaka. I will send you the materials.

g2|20|〜ないで|Do something without doing something else.|Vない + で + action|Contrast なくて for a reason: 食べないで出た means left without eating; 食べなくて困った describes a problem caused by not eating.|朝ご飯を食べないで出かけました。|I went out without eating breakfast.

g2|20|文の中の疑問・という名前|Embed questions and name things.|Question clause + か; yes/no clause + かどうか; name + という + N|An embedded question stays inside the larger sentence. Noun and な-adjective predicates usually omit だ before か.|電車が何時に来るか分かりません。|I do not know what time the train comes.

g2|20|〜やすい・〜にくい|Easy or difficult to do.|Vます-stem + やすい / にくい|These behave as い-adjectives. They can describe tendencies as well as a person's subjective ease.|このペンは書きやすいです。|This pen is easy to write with.

g2|21|受身|Describe receiving an action.|U-verbs a-row + れる; ru-verbs stem + られる; する→される、来る→来られる|The affected person/thing becomes the subject. Some passives convey inconvenience, but not every passive is negative.|この本は多くの人に読まれています。|This book is read by many people.

g2|21|形容詞＋する・〜てほしい|Cause a state; want someone to act.|い-adjectiveくする; な-adjective/Nにする; person に Vてほしい|する describes deliberately making a change; なる describes becoming. てほしい states a wish about someone else's action and may sound direct.|音を小さくしてください。少し待ってほしいです。|Please turn the sound down. I would like you to wait a little.

g2|22|使役・使役＋授受|Make, let or allow someone to do something.|U-verbs a-row + せる; ru-verbs stem + させる; する→させる、来る→来させる|Context distinguishes coercion and permission. Causative + てもらう/てくれる often describes receiving permission. Check に/を according to transitivity.|先生が私に発表させてくれました。|The teacher let me give a presentation.

g2|22|〜なさい|An instruction from someone with authority.|Vます-stem + なさい|Common from a parent or teacher to a child. It is not a general polite request to a superior. Negative dictionary + な is a prohibition.|名前をここに書きなさい。|Write your name here.

g2|22|〜のような・〜のように|Resemblance modifying a noun or action.|Nのような + N; Nのように + predicate|ような modifies a noun; ように modifies a verb or adjective. This is distinct from purpose ように.|雪のように白い花が咲いています。|Flowers as white as snow are blooming.

g2|23|使役受身|Be made to do something.|Full causative + られる; some u-verbs contract to a-row + される|書かせられる can contract to 書かされる. す-ending verbs do not use the same contraction: 話させられる. する→させられる.|子供の頃、毎日野菜を食べさせられました。|As a child I was made to eat vegetables every day.

g2|23|〜ことにしている|Maintain a personal rule.|V dictionary / Vない + ことにしている|A continuing personal policy. Contrast ことになっている for a rule, arrangement or schedule presented as externally established.|寝る前にスマホを見ないことにしています。|I make it a rule not to look at my phone before bed.

g2|23|〜まで・〜方|Until a boundary; how to do something.|V dictionary / N + まで; Vます-stem + 方|まで marks continuation up to a boundary; までに is a deadline. 読み方 means how to read; する compounds use Nの仕方.|雨がやむまで待ちます。この字の読み方を教えてください。|I will wait until the rain stops. Please tell me how to read this character.

n3|4|〜一方で・〜というより|Contrast coexisting aspects or choose a more accurate description.|Plain clause + 一方で; AというよりB|一方で can contrast two aspects or groups. というより replaces an initial description with a better one, rather than merely adding another fact.|この部屋は狭いというより、物が多すぎるのです。|Rather than the room being small, it has too many things in it.

n3|5|〜によって・〜による：原因|A cause or means, depending on context.|Nによって + predicate; Nによる + N|Unlike the variation use, causal によって identifies what brought about a result. The same form can also mark means or the agent of a passive.|強風によって木が倒れました。|A tree fell because of the strong wind.

n3|6|〜なら・〜ば・〜たら|Select a conditional to match the relation between clauses.|Plain form + なら; conditional ば; past form + ら|なら takes up a premise and can give advice before the action. たら can mean after completion. ば describes a sufficient condition; restrictions on requests depend on predicates and subjects.|京都に行くなら、先にホテルを予約したほうがいいです。|If you are going to Kyoto, you should book a hotel first.

n3|7|〜ということだ・〜とのことだ|Report information received.|Plain clause + ということだ / とのことだ|A formal way to relay news or a message. ということだ can also express an interpretation, so identify whether there is an information source.|連絡によると、会議は延期されたとのことです。|According to the message, the meeting has been postponed.

n3|7|〜と言われている|Report a widespread view.|Plain clause + と言われている|The passive presents what people commonly say, without identifying a particular speaker. It does not itself prove the claim.|この町は住みやすいと言われています。|This town is said to be easy to live in.

n3|7|〜とか・〜って・〜という|Informal reports, quotations and labels.|Plain clause + とか / って; name or clause + というN|とか can relay uncertain information; って is casual. という links a name or content to a following noun. Do not confuse hearsay とか with listing AとかBとか.|田中さんは来月引っ越すとか。|I hear Tanaka is moving next month.

n3|8|〜ことは〜が|Concede a point with a reservation.|V/い-adjective + ことは + same predicate + が|Repeat the predicate: 読んだことは読んだが admits reading while qualifying what that means. It does not deny the action happened.|読んだことは読みましたが、全部は理解できませんでした。|I did read it, but I could not understand all of it.

n3|9|〜てもらいたい・〜てほしい|Want another person to do something.|Person に Vてもらいたい / Vてほしい|てもらいたい frames the wish as receiving a favor; てほしい directly describes the desired action. Negative wishes use Vないでほしい.|先生に作文を確認してもらいたいです。|I would like my teacher to check my composition.

n3|9|〜させてもらいたい|Want permission to do something.|Causativeて + もらいたい / いただきたい / ほしい|The speaker wants to be allowed to act. いただきたい is more deferential; permission and benefit should be relevant, not merely a decorative honorific.|次の会議で私にも発表させていただきたいです。|I would also like permission to present at the next meeting.

n3|9|〜といい・〜ばいい・〜たらいい|Express a hope or suggest a solution.|Plain non-past + といい; conditional ば/たら + いい|In a wish, the desired outcome is not presented as fully under the speaker's control. The same forms can also give advice, depending on context.|明日は晴れるといいですね。|I hope it is sunny tomorrow.

n3|10|命令・禁止・〜こと|Direct instructions and written rules.|U-verb e-row; ru-verb stem+ろ; する→しろ; V dictionary+な; V dictionary/ない+こと|Imperatives and Vな prohibitions are strong. Sentence-final こと often appears in written instructions and rules. It is not the same as nominalizing a verb.|試験中は辞書を使わないこと。|Do not use a dictionary during the exam.

n3|10|〜たらどうか|Suggest a course of action.|Vた + らどうか / らどうですか|Usually advice to someone else. Tone and relationship determine whether it sounds supportive or critical.|一度、先生に相談したらどうですか。|Why not consult your teacher once?

n3|12|謙譲語II・丁寧語|Distinguish listener-oriented modest speech from polite endings.|申す・参る・おります; です・ます・ございます|謙譲語I respects the person an action is directed toward; 謙譲語II is modest speech toward the listener. 丁寧語 marks politeness without changing who acts.|私は駅の近くに住んでおります。|I live near the station. (Modest/polite)

n3|A|助詞の整理：も・しか・くらい・まで|Identify what a particle adds to the sentence.|Nも; Nしか + negative; quantityくらい; Nまで|も can mean also or as many as; くらい can give an approximate amount or a minimal example; まで can mean even. Read the predicate before deciding the sense.|子供までそのニュースを知っています。|Even children know that news.

n3|B|について・に対して・にとって・として|Topic, target, perspective and role.|Nについて / に対して / にとって / として|について identifies a topic; に対して a target or contrast; にとって an evaluating perspective; として a role. The following predicate helps decide which fits.|教師として、学生に対して公平でありたいです。|As a teacher, I want to be fair toward students.

n3|C|こと・の・もの|Nominalize events and distinguish things from facts.|Plain clause + こと/の; concrete thing + もの|Perception constructions often use の: 走るのを見た. Fixed patterns such as ことができる require こと. Do not assume the nominalizers are interchangeable everywhere.|毎日歩くことは大切です。子供が走るのを見ました。|Walking every day is important. I saw a child running.

n3|D|ようだ・ように：比喩・目的・指示|Distinguish resemblance, a goal and an indirect instruction.|Nのようだ; V dictionary/ない + ように; Vようにと言う|ように can describe resemblance, a desired outcome, or the content of an instruction. With a goal, non-volitional/potential or negative forms are common; ために often expresses a controlled purpose.|忘れないように、メモするように言われました。|I was told to take notes so that I would not forget.

n3|E|わけだ・ないわけにはいかない|A logical conclusion; being unable not to act.|Plain clause + わけだ; Vない + わけにはいかない|わけだ connects facts into an explanation. The double negative ないわけにはいかない expresses an obligation, not a prohibition.|約束したので、行かないわけにはいきません。|Since I promised, I have to go.

n3|F|ばかり：偏り・追加・直後|Only, repeatedly, not only, or just finished.|Nばかり; Vてばかりいる; ばかりでなく; V dictionaryばかりだ; Vたばかりだ|Identify the form before ばかり. たばかり is subjectively recent; たところ emphasizes the immediate phase after completion. Repeated-action てばかりいる often conveys criticism.|弟はゲームをしてばかりいます。私は帰ったばかりです。|My younger brother does nothing but play games. I have only just returned.

n3|G|する・なる：変化・習慣・決定|Distinguish making a change from a change happening.|Adjく/に + する/なる; Vことにする/なる; Vようにする/なる|する emphasizes a deliberate choice or effort. なる describes a resulting change or arrangement. ようになっている can describe how a system is designed.|毎日練習して、日本語で話せるようになりました。|By practicing every day, I became able to speak in Japanese.

n3|H|条件形の特別な用法|Discovery, narrative sequence and adding characteristics.|Vと…た; Vたら…た; Nも…ばNも…|Past と/たら may describe an actual discovery rather than a hypothetical condition. も…ば…も adds two features; it need not express an if-then relation.|窓を開けると、猫がいました。この店は安くもあれば、おいしくもあります。|When I opened the window, there was a cat. This restaurant is both inexpensive and tasty.

n3|I|副詞と文末の呼応|Match adverbs to the meaning of the ending.|決して + negative; まるで + ようだ; たとえ + ても; 必ずしも + negative|Look beyond the blank. 必ずしも否定 means not necessarily, whereas 決して否定 is emphatic rejection. まさか often signals disbelief.|高い物が必ずしも丈夫だとは限りません。|Expensive things are not necessarily durable.

n3|J|複合動詞・接尾辞|Expand a verb or noun's meaning with a suffix.|V-stem + 始める/続ける/終わる/出す/切る; N + らしい/っぽい|Suffixes differ in meaning and attachment. 出す can describe a sudden onset; 始める is a general start. らしい can mean typical of; っぽい often marks a resemblance or tendency.|雨が降り出しましたが、最後まで走り切りました。|It suddenly started raining, but I ran all the way to the end.

n2|1|〜際に|On the occasion of doing something.|V dictionary/た + 際に; Nの際に|More formal than とき. Common in instructions and notices. The form before 際 depends on whether the event is prospective or completed.|申請する際に、身分証を持参してください。|Please bring identification when applying.

n2|2|〜うちに・〜ようとしている|While a condition lasts; just about to change.|V dictionary/ない/ている + うちに; volitional + としている|うちに can signal a chance before a condition changes. ようとしている can describe an imminent change, even without a human intention.|日が暮れようとしています。明るいうちに帰りましょう。|The sun is about to set. Let us return while it is light.

n2|2|〜つつ・〜つつも|Simultaneous action or acting despite awareness.|Vます-stem + つつ / つつも|The simultaneous use is relatively formal and shares a subject. Concessive つつ often contrasts what someone knows or thinks with what they do.|悪いと知りつつ、約束を破ってしまいました。|Although I knew it was wrong, I broke my promise.

n2|3|〜次第：時間|As soon as a prerequisite is completed.|Vます-stem + 次第|Common in plans, announcements and requests. It normally introduces an intended subsequent action, rather than narrating an accidental past sequence.|結果が分かり次第、ご連絡します。|I will contact you as soon as I know the result.

n2|3|〜て以来・〜てこのかた|A state continuing since an event.|Vて + 以来 / このかた; N以来|The initial event is a starting boundary and the following state continues through the relevant period. Do not use it merely for one unrelated event afterward.|引っ越して以来、毎朝歩いています。|Since moving, I have been walking every morning.
